w: At 11.10 am, the head of Namdhari Sikh Sampradaya, Sadguru Jagjitsinh and his disciples came to meet Swamishri. During their dialogue the practice and belief of Guru being the way to God was discussed.

At 5.47 pm Swamishri arrived to inaugurate the site for the new Swaminarayan mandir. The youths and devotees of Toronto Satsang Chapter had created 'Swaminarayan Nagar', comprising of an artistic archway, exhibition, cultural spots, assembly hall, landscape and kitchen facilities. After Vedic chantings Swamishri inaugurated the Swaminarayan Nagar and visited the exhibition - 'Pathways to Harmony'. Swamishri finally blessed the evening assembly.

Devotion to Thakorji Despite Swamishri's old age, he always grasps the opportunity of offering devotion to Thakorji in any form. Today, after his morning puja Swamishri came for Thakorji's darshan at the Swaminarayan mandir. He asked for the mattress to be laid. The attendant sadhus were surprised as to why Swamishri wished to perform prostrations. It was not Ekadashi or neither was he taking leave - two occasions when Swamishri offers prostrations before the Lord. When Swamishri was asked, he remained silent. After performing the prostrations Swamishri said, "Because the Hindola Festival has started today."

Murti Pratishtha In the morning, Swamishri performed the Vedic murti-pratishta in the haveli, and for the first time outside of India, consecrated a murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni to which people can offer abhishek. During the murti-pratishtha assembly, Swamishri described the glory of mandirs and the newly consecrated murtis. He explained that the more darshan one has of these murtis, the more peace one will experience. In the evening assembly, Shri Ramesh Oza and Shri Bhagwat were in attendance. They both addressed the assembly and greeted Swamishri.

An already beautiful Haveli complex was made even more stunning with the addition of brilliant new murtis and an intricately carved new sinhaasan in Toronto. In the morning, Swamishri performed the Murti Pratishtha Vidhi for the murtis, and for the first time outside of India, he consecrated a golden murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni. People can perform an "abhishek" for this murti, which is an offering of water.

During the morning assembly, Swamishri described the glory of mandirs as well as the newly consecrated murtis. He explained that the more darshan one has of these murtis, the more peace one will experience.
In the evening assembly, Sant Shri Rameshbhai Oza and Shri Bhagwatbhai were in attendance. They both addressed the assembly and greeted Swamishri.

ds.t: Done by command, it is all a mala
w: Monday, 18 July 2005 (Ashadh sud 11, Samvat 2061), Delhi

In the evening, after his walk and yoga postures, while Pramukh Swami Maharaj was taking prasad, Harshadbhai Chavda, seated in front, said, "When you were inspecting Akshardham, after that I had a wish in my mind to tell you that the spire has gone up on Akshardham. Now give me the mala, so that I do nothing else but turn the mala."

Hearing this, Swamishri said, "Whatever is done by command is itself a mala. Every stone you move is a mala. There is no objection to turning the mala in puja or in some other way, but there are still mandirs to be built, so what we do by command is itself called a mala. Meditation is to be done, but the work of seva is considered greater than meditation. Meditation has been done in the Sampradaya from the very beginning, but at the time of doing seva for God, meditation should be put to one side. If there is seva to be done and one goes off to meditate, body-consciousness increases and the seva of God and the Sant does not get done. When devotees have come, we have to look after them and feed them, go ourselves, get up; at such times meditation should take second place."

Guru Purnima celebration was celebrated in Bochasan in the presence of Swamishri and thousands of devotees. Senior sadhus praised the saintliness of Swamishri. The mammoth assembly climaxed with Swamishri’s blessings. (Details in August issue of Swaminarayan Bliss, p.16.)

Over 30,000 devotees attended the Guru Purnima Celebration in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Bochasan on 18 July 2008.

The celebration assembly began at 8.00 am with dhun and bhajans. Thereafter senior sadhus - Ishwarcharan Swami, Doctor Swami and Mahant Swami - spoke about how to offer devotion to guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj by obeying his wishes and realizing his spiritual purity.
Thereafter, children, teenagers and youths performed a traditional dance honoring God and guru. Then Swamishri was honored with garlands by the senior sadhus, on behalf of all devotees worldwide.
Finally, blessing the assembly Swamishri talked about the four endeavors of human life - dharma, artha (prosperity), kama (desires) and moksha (redemption) and the need for satsang in attaining them.
